TM-RF-15-002 Rev. A · C-band 6×6 array · Results and project status

1Summary of results

5.35–6.26 GHzPresent element matched (VSWR ≤ 3): 16 % bandwidth
54 %Bandwidth required for 4–7 GHz
8.7–9.8 dBiElement gain (accepted power), 5–6.5 GHz
> 20 dBIsolation between V and H inputs over most of the band (array)
Main result. The poor input match reported on the array is caused by the radiating element itself, whose matched bandwidth is about 16 %, well below the 54 % needed for 4–7 GHz. The radiator works correctly inside its band, which is why the gain is as expected while the VSWR is poor.
Consequence. A change to the feed network alone cannot bring the VSWR below 3:1 across 4–7 GHz. A new wideband radiating element is required; its development has started (section 5).
Measured panel. Bench measurements confirm the input-match behaviour and show a gain of 20.4 dBi peak, about 3 dB below the 23 dBi rating, with a strong drop above 6 GHz (section 6).

The element is matched only between 5.35 and 6.26 GHz. Outside this window the realised gain falls because of the mismatch, while the gain referred to accepted power stays at 8.7–9.8 dBi.

TM-RF-15-002 Rev. A · C-band 6×6 array · Results and project status

4Complete array results (preliminary)

  • Both inputs are best in the middle of the band (about 5.0–6.2 GHz).
  • Below about 4.8 GHz and above about 6.3 GHz both inputs are mostly at VSWR 3:1 or worse, consistent with the element result.
  • Isolation between the V and H inputs is better than 20 dB over most of the band.
  • The array result confirms that the element bandwidth is the limiting factor.

5Element development (in progress)

A new wideband element is being developed to meet VSWR < 3 (target < 2) over the full 4–7 GHz band on both polarisations. Iteration 1 has been completed; it is matched from 4.95 to 5.75 GHz and has defined the design direction for iteration 2.

* nearest S11 marker (5.7 / 5.9 GHz). Gain by substitution against a reference horn at ~5 m. Port A/B to V/H mapping and radome condition during the gain test to be confirmed.

  • The measured input match agrees with the predicted array response: best in the middle of the band, poorer at the band edges.
  • Measured peak gain is 20.4 dBi (V) and 20.0 dBi (H), about 3 dB below the 23 dBi rating.
  • Gain drops to 11–15 dBi at 6.2–6.4 GHz. The input mismatch accounts for at most about 1.5 dB of this; the cause of the remaining drop is under investigation.

8Actions requested from the client

  • Confirm the required specification: VSWR limit (3:1 or 2:1), band edges, gain and isolation targets.
  • Confirm any mechanical constraints for the new element (total height, materials, array size and pitch).
  • Confirm which panel port is V and which is H, and whether the gain was measured with the radome fitted.
  • If possible, repeat the gain measurement with and without the radome, and provide pattern cuts at 5.5 and 6.4 GHz.
